15.solution: An aromatic aldehyde has the CHO group bonded directly to the benzene ring. In structure D (2-methylbenzaldehyde) it is. In A and B the CHO is on a side chain (phenylacetaldehyde, cinnamaldehyde), and C has a cyclohexane ring, not a benzene ring.

16.solution: Running through both ethyl groups gives the longest chain, nine carbons, containing the C=C and the C-OH. Numbering from the end nearer the OH puts it on C-4, the double bond at C-5 and methyl groups on C-3 and C-7: 3,7-dimethylnon-5-en-4-ol.

39.solution: Cadmium has a full \(4d^{10}\) set in the atom and in its only common ion \(\mathrm{Cd^{2+}}\), so it is not a transition element. Cu and Au have ions with incomplete d orbitals, and Sc has \(3d^1\).

46.solution: Lactose is galactose + glucose, and raffinose is galactose + glucose + fructose. Sucrose and maltose contain no galactose.

Nylon-6,6 (D) is made by condensing adipic acid with hexamethylenediamine, with loss of water. Teflon and polythene are addition polymers.

Nylon-6 (C), made from caprolactam, is also listed among condensation polymers (polyamides) in the textbooks, so the question has two correct options.

54.solution: At \(\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\) the line reads \(a + b + c = 0\), true for every member of the family.

55.subtopic: Slopes of a Homogeneous Pair — Sum, Product and Ratio Conditions
55.solution: The slopes satisfy \(m_1 + m_2 = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}\) and \(m_1m_2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). So \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{(1 + \sqrt{3})/\sqrt{3}}{1 - 1/\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}\).

56.subtopic: Tangents — At a Point, With a Given Slope, From an External Point and Their Loci
56.solution: \(OP = 10\) and each tangent has length \(\sqrt{100 - r^2}\), so the area is \(2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}r\sqrt{100 - r^2} = r\sqrt{100 - r^2}\). This is greatest when \(r^2 = 100 - r^2\), that is \(r = 5\sqrt{2}\).

57.subtopic: Equation of a Circle — Centre-Radius, General, Diameter and Parametric Forms
57.solution: The tangent to the parabola at \((1, 1)\) has slope 2, so the centre lies on the normal there: \((1 - 2t, 1 + t)\). Equal distances to \((1, 1)\) and \((0, 1)\): \(5t^2 = (1 - 2t)^2 + t^2\), so \(t = \dfrac{1}{4}\) and the centre is \(\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)\).

59.subtopic: Algebraic Limits — Factorisation, Rationalisation and the xⁿ − aⁿ Form
59.solution:
The denominator is \((x - 1)^2\), so the numerator p must have a double root at 1: \(p(1) = 1 + a + b + c = 0\) and \(p'(1) = 3 + 2a + b = 0\). The limit is then \(\dfrac{p''(1)}{2} = 3 + a = 2026\).

So \(a = 2023\), \(b = -4049\), \(c = 2025\), and \(a - c = -2\).

60.subtopic: Finding Truth Values of Component Statements
60.solution:
The implication is false only when the left side is T and \(p \wedge q\) is F. \(\sim r\) T gives r F; \(q \to r\) T then needs q F; \(p \vee q\) T then needs p T. So p T, q F, r F.

Then \(p \to q\) is F, \(p \to r\) is F and \((\sim p) \wedge r\) is F, as claimed. But \((\sim q) \to p = \mathrm{T} \to \mathrm{T} = \mathrm{T}\), so (C) is not true.

61.solution: (A) and (B) have false antecedents, so they are true; (D) is true since \(\sim q\) is T. In (C), \((\sim p \vee q) \wedge \sim r = \mathrm{F}\) while p is T, so the biconditional is false.

62.subtopic: Finding Truth Values of Component Statements
62.solution: \(\sim p \to q\) is false only when \(\sim p\) is T and q is F: p F, q F. Then \(q \leftrightarrow r\) false needs r T.

63.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Half-Angle Formulas, Napier's Analogy and Area
63.solution: The product is \(16\Delta^2 = 16 \cdot \dfrac{1}{4}b^2c^2\sin^2 A = 4b^2c^2\sin^2 A\). So \(\sin^2 A = \dfrac{3}{4}\) and A is \(60^\circ\) or \(120^\circ\).

64.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Half-Angle Formulas, Napier's Analogy and Area
64.solution: The expression is \(\dfrac{1 - \cos A}{1 + \cos A} = \tan^2\dfrac{A}{2}\). With \(s = 4\): \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{(s - b)(s - c)}{\Delta} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{3}{2}}{\Delta} = \dfrac{3}{4\Delta}\), so the value is \(\left(\dfrac{3}{4\Delta}\right)^2\).

65.subtopic: Determinants, Cofactors and the Adjoint Identities
65.solution: \(\mathrm{adj}(A^{-1}) = |A^{-1}|(A^{-1})^{-1} = \dfrac{A}{|A|}\). \(|A| = (-1)(2)(-1) = 2\), and the elements of A add to 6078, so the sum is 3039.

66.solution: \(AB = I\). Row 3 of A with column 3 of \(37B\): \(11 + 28 + k = 37\), so \(k = -2\).

67.solution: Principal values: \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\) and \(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). The sum is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).

68.subtopic: Composite Functions — f∘g, Iteration and Functional Identities
68.solution:
\(f(f(x)) = \dfrac{-1}{x - 1}\) and \(f(f(f(x))) = x\), so the compositions repeat every 3. \(2025\) is a multiple of 3, so \(g_{2025}(x) = x\), and \(g_{2026}(x) = f(x) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{x}\).

\(\displaystyle\int x\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)dx = \int x\,dx - x\), so \(h(x) = -x\).

75.subtopic: Rolle's Theorem and Mean Value Theorem
75.solution:
\(f(\alpha) = f(\alpha + 3) = 0\), so \(f(x) = (x - \alpha)(x - \alpha - 3)\) and Rolle's point is \(c = \alpha + \dfrac{3}{2}\).

For g, \(g(\beta) = g(3) = 0\), so \(\beta\) and 3 are the roots of \((x - \alpha)(x - \alpha - 3) = -2\), which are \(\alpha + 1\) and \(\alpha + 2\). Hence \(\beta = \alpha + 1\) and \(3 = \alpha + 2\), giving \(\alpha = 1\), \(\beta = 2\); the two Rolle points are both \(\dfrac{5}{2}\), as required.

\(f(x) = (x - 1)(x - 4)\), \(g(1) = f(1) + 2 = 2\), and \((f \circ g)(1) = f(2) = (1)(-2) = -2\).

76.subtopic: Rate of Change and Related Rates
76.solution: \(\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 8\pi r\dfrac{dr}{dt}\) and \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}\), so \(\dfrac{dV/dt}{dS/dt} = \dfrac{r}{2} = \dfrac{10}{5}\) and \(r = 4\) cm.

79.subtopic: Modulus and Greatest-Integer Integrands — Split the Interval
79.solution: Split at \(x = \dfrac{3}{5}\): \(\displaystyle\int_0^{3/5}(3 - 5x)\,dx = \dfrac{9}{10}\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{3/5}^{1}(5x - 3)\,dx = \dfrac{4}{10}\). The total is \(\dfrac{13}{10}\).

80.solution: \(\dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} = \dfrac{e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-x}}\), whose integral is \(-\log(1 + e^{-x})\). From 0 to \(\infty\): \(0 - (-\log 2) = \log 2\).

81.subtopic: Evaluating Definite Integrals — Standard Forms, Algebraic Substitution and By Parts
81.solution: \(f(5) - f(2) = \displaystyle\int_2^5\dfrac{x + 1}{\sqrt{x - 1}}dx\). With \(t = \sqrt{x - 1}\), \(x = t^2 + 1\), \(dx = 2t\,dt\), t from 1 to 2: \(\displaystyle\int_1^2 2(t^2 + 2)\,dt = 2\left[\dfrac{t^3}{3} + 2t\right]_1^2 = 2\left(\dfrac{7}{3} + 2\right) = \dfrac{26}{3}\).

82.subtopic: Area Under a Curve — Between a Curve and an Axis
82.solution: The curve meets the axis at 0 and 2: \(\displaystyle\int_0^2(2x - x^2)\,dx = 4 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\).

83.subtopic: Area Between Two Curves — Intersections First
83.solution:
The curves meet where \(x^2 + 8x = 9\), at \(x = 1\). By symmetry the area is twice the part above the axis: \(2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^1\sqrt{8x}\,dx + \int_1^3\sqrt{9 - x^2}\,dx\right]\).

\(\displaystyle\int_0^1 2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{x}\,dx = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}\) and \(\displaystyle\int_1^3\sqrt{9 - x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{9\pi}{4} - \sqrt{2} - \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}\). Doubling gives option (A).

84.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
84.solution: The lines \(x\cos\alpha + y\sin\alpha = p\) have two arbitrary constants, so the equation is of second order. Every straight line has constant slope, so \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\).

85.solution:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{6x^2}{1 + x^3}y = \dfrac{1 + x^2}{1 + x^3}\) has integrating factor \((1 + x^3)^2\). Then \(y(1 + x^3)^2 = \displaystyle\int(1 + x^2)(1 + x^3)\,dx = x + \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^4}{4} + \dfrac{x^6}{6} + c\).

So \(s = 2\) and \(p, q, r\) are 3, 4, 6; their LCM is 12.

86.solution: Put \(v = x + y\): \(\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + \cos v = 2\cos^2\dfrac{v}{2}\). Then \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\dfrac{v}{2}\,dv = x + c\), that is \(\tan\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = x + c\).

89.solution: \(\begin{vmatrix} 2a & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & a & -a \\ 3 & a & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 2a(a^2) + (0 - 3a) = 2a^3 - 3a\), so the volume is \(V = 3a - 2a^3\) on \([0, 1]\). \(V' = 3 - 6a^2 = 0\) at \(a = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), where \(V = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\).

\(OA = \sqrt{5}\) and \(OB = \sqrt{10}\), so D divides AB in the ratio \(AD : DB = 1 : \sqrt{2}\): \(\vec{OD} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\vec{A} + \vec{B}}{1 + \sqrt{2}}\).

With \(\vec{AB} = (2, 1)\): \(\vec{A}\cdot\vec{AB} = 0\) and \(\vec{B}\cdot\vec{AB} = 5\), so \(\vec{OD}\cdot\vec{AB} = \dfrac{5}{1 + \sqrt{2}} = 5(\sqrt{2} - 1)\).

113.solution: Heat lost by the warm water equals heat to melt the ice and warm it: \(60(40 - T) = 15 \times 80 + 15T\), so \(2400 - 60T = 1200 + 15T\) and \(T = 16\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}\).

114.solution: With no work, \(dU = dQ < 0\): the internal energy, and with it the temperature, decreases (at constant volume the pressure falls too).
